fail_samples.text_head: NTA AND INVESTMENT UPDATE September 2026 The CDO share price and NTA went ex-dividend on 29 September 2026 for the 7.5 cps fully franked final dividend, resulting in the post-tax NTA being $2.137 at the end of September. Before the dividend was paid, the post-tax NTA was $2.212, in line with the $2.21 issue price of the SPP and placement. Fund Performance Cadence Opportunities Fund was down 4.9% in September, compared to the All Ordinaries Accumulation Index which was down 2.5% for the month. For the first quarter of the financial year, the portfolio was down 2.4%, compared to the All Ordinaries Accumulation Index which was up 1.0% for the quarter. CDO’s share price over the past quarter, including dividends and franking, was up 8.1%, and for the year was up 32.0%. The largest detractors from performance during the first quarter were Lindian Resources, Guzman Y Gomez, EchoIQ, Pro Medicus, Life360, and Liontown. The top contributors were Turaco Gold, CSL, Kantra Copper, Many Peaks Minerals, Generation Development Group, Metals X and Ringcentral. Lindian Resources is developing its Kangankunde rare earth project in Malawi which it expects to ramp up through 2027. During the period, Lindian’s share price fell 47% following two key developments: the announcement of an offtake agreement with French downstream specialist Carestar and proposed amendments to the Malawi Mining Code. CDO reduced its exposure to Lindian during the period. We maintain a position with the view that the government will act rationally, and the proposed mine will proceed. For more information contact Cadence Opportunities Fund on 02 8298 2450 or email info@cadencecapital.com.au Register to receive our newsletter at www.cadencecapital.com.au/register-for-free-newsletter ylno esu lanosrep roF Other detractors included EchoIQ and Guzman Y Gomez. EchoIQ specialises in artificial intelligence solutions for cardiovascular diagnostics. During the period, the fund re-entered EchoIQ after trading it successfully earlier in 2026. The fund entered this position prior to FDA approval which did not occur in the first instance. A meeting with the FDA in connection with EIQ’s appeal is expected to occur within the next 30 days. Having successfully shorted Guzman Y Gomez during the last financial year, the fund closed its remaining short position during this quarter. Core positions in Turaco Gold, CSL, Kantra Copper and Many Peaks performed well during the period. Interest rates set by the Reserve Bank and longer-term yields set by the bond market, rose substantially over the past quarter. Some of the factors driving higher interest rates are global government deficits and the flow- on impact that it has on inflation through elevated government spending. This backdrop provides a tailwind for gold positions in the fund. Turaco Gold and Many Peaks are two such examples. Our top performing stock for the quarter, Turaco Gold is advancing towards the release of its Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS), a key deliverable prior to first production, with the company also considered a takeover target for mid and large cap gold companies in the region. Many Peaks continues to return high grade gold hits from drilling at its Ferke project in Côte d’Ivoire, which will enable it to expand upon its recently released maiden gold Resource of 1.3Moz. Higher interest rates impacting valuations have also created opportunities to initiate new long positions. Some stocks that were once expensive and did not meet our investment criteria began to meet our criteria during the period following abrupt sell-offs. CSL is one such example. The poorly executed acquisition of Vifor in 2025, along with several downgrades to its foundational plasma business through 2026 resulted in the stock falling from over $300 per share to less than $100 per share earlier this year. During the month, modular data centre manufacturer and operator DXN (ASX: DXN) and Network-as-a-Service provider Megaport (ASX: MP1) were both contributors to the investment portfolio performance. DXN is a modular data centre manufacturer and operator, scaled across the Asia-Pacific region. The company’s share price increased 53% in September, as investors continued to respond positively to the company's FY2026 full year result, released at the end of August. The result highlighted a record order backlog and growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related data centre infrastructure.
